category_title: Students performing as rhythmic, collaborative poetry readers
minimal_context: Bill and Kwame are demonstrating how they read a poem together during the whole class share session at the conclusion of the reading workshop.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please demonstrate how you read the poem together for the class.

STUDENT: (In singing voices) Kwame: This is the way / Bill: Hey! / Kwame: we start the day / Bill: Hey!

TUTOR: Okay, continue reading the rest of it.

STUDENT: (Continuing in singing voices) Kwame: we get the knowledge / Bill: Hey! / Kwame: to go to college / Bill: Hey! / Kwame: we won’t stop there / Bill: Hey! / Kwame: go anywhere / Bill: Hey!

TUTOR: You are done performing. What kind of a cheer do you want?

STUDENT: Kwame: A poem cheer. / Bill: (swinging his poetry packet over his head) Don’t hurt the poems!

options.A: Use the poem as an entry point to focus mainly on using language to support meaning rather than sentence structure.
options.B: Clarify any misconceptions in their reading steps and re-teach the procedural skills to the students when necessary.
options.C: Teach mindfulness principles, mindfulness exercises, and reflective poems to the students during the share session.
options.D: Draw a page in the air, pretend to write, and take a sip from an imaginary cappuccino.
